summary: CBS Sports' Dave Richard goes game by game through the Week 13 2023 NFL slate, naming fantasy football starts, sits and sleepers with matchup reasoning and stats. He stresses matchups over draft position and promotes his SportsLine strength-of-schedule rankings. Detailed player write-ups cover DK Metcalf, Tyler Lockett, Russell Wilson, Chris Godwin, Amari Cooper and Cooper Kupp, among others.
one_line: Dave Richard's Week 13 2023 fantasy football guide gives game-by-game starts, sits and sleepers based on matchups, injuries and recent trends.
key_facts: Dave Richard argues fantasy lineup decisions should depend on weekly matchups rather than the order players were drafted.
Richard is updating projected Strength of Schedule rankings by position on SportsLine; promo code RICHARD gives the first month for a dollar.
In Seahawks-Cowboys, only two QBs have exceeded 250 yards against Dallas this year, and Curtis Samuel was the first receiver to reach 100 yards on the Cowboys (12 targets, 9 catches).

DK Metcalf has at least nine targets in each of his past three games, but has caught just three of 12 targets traveling 15-plus Air Yards over the past four weeks; he faces cornerback DaRon Bland, who has seven interceptions.
Richard says to sit Jake Ferguson because Seattle has allowed only one touchdown to a tight end all season (David Njoku, Week 8) and Dallas is a 9-point favorite.
Russell Wilson leads in TD rate at 6.3% with a 68.3% completion rate, but averages only 29 attempts per game; Richard expects a 20-plus point game against Houston, where QBs average 34.8 attempts.
Seven straight quarterbacks facing the Broncos failed to reach 20 fantasy points, including Josh Allen once and Patrick Mahomes twice.
Devin Singletary played 81% of Houston's snaps last week and Denver has allowed 5.4 yards per carry over its past six games.

The Lions rank league-worst in defensive EPA per dropback (-0.40); New Orleans is missing Rashid Shaheed (thigh) and Chris Olave is in concussion protocol, and Alvin Kamara led targets per route run (30.8%).
Chris Godwin has been under 60 yards in five straight games, has one touchdown despite nine end-zone targets, and lines up wide on 68% of his snaps; Richard says to sit him.
Amari Cooper should benefit from new Browns QB Joe Flacco, who threw 15-plus Air Yards passes on 20 percent of his throws with the Jets; Cooper's ADOT fell to 7.57 yards from 15.42 in recent games.
Cooper Kupp looked hurt in Week 12 and has just 13 targets in his past three games, so Richard sits him against the Browns.
Since acquiring Chase Young, the 49ers have allowed 30 points in three games, with 15 sacks and four interceptions.
Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's unit blitzed on nearly 50% of snaps against the Eagles and Raiders, and Richard expects L'Jarius Sneed to cover Christian Watson most.
